name: Server Hardware Variation
description: Servers are unlikely to be perfectly identical. Subtle variations in CPU clock speeds, memory latency, or cache sizes can lead to differing processing times for coin flips and updates to the counter, resulting in multimodal latency distributions. This is a very common source of variance in distributed systems.

name: Coin Generation Algorithm Timing Variations
description: The algorithm used to generate the 'heads' or 'tails' result on each server will inherently have slight timing variations. Even if the algorithm is perfectly deterministic in theory, the timing of operations within the algorithm can produce variations due to scheduling and other factors, especially across different server CPUs.

name: Network Latency Fluctuations
description: Communication between the controller and the servers introduces network latency, which is rarely constant. Variations in network congestion, routing paths, and physical distances can cause significant fluctuations in response times. The controller's decision-making also contributes to latency.

name: Server Load Variations
description: If the servers are running other processes concurrently, their utilization can change, affecting the time available for coin flips and counter updates. Even small spikes in load can introduce variability.

name: Controller Processing Time
description: The time taken by the controller to make decisions (choosing which server to contact, processing the response) contributes to the overall latency. This will be influenced by the controller’s CPU load and any other processes it's running.

name: Operating System Scheduling Variations
description: The OS scheduling algorithm on each server will influence when tasks (coin flip generation, counter update) are executed. Differences in these scheduling decisions will introduce timing variations.

name: Clock Drift Between Servers
description: Even small differences in the clocks of the two servers can accumulate over time, especially with intermittent updates. While less likely, this could contribute to the latency distribution.

name: Coin Generation Seed Variability (If Applicable)
description: If the coin generation uses a seed value, slight differences in the initial seed can lead to different outcomes, affecting the distribution.

name: Interrupt Handling Latency
description: Variations in how the servers handle interrupts (e.g., from the controller's requests) can contribute to timing differences.

name: Memory Access Patterns
description: Differences in how the servers access memory for the counter and coin flip data can introduce variations in processing times.

name: Cache Misses
description: Differences in cache utilization due to the nature of the data being accessed could contribute to variations.

name: Power Supply Variations
description: Minor fluctuations in power supply voltages can impact CPU clock speeds and, therefore, processing times.

name: Firmware Version Differences
description: Slight differences in the firmware versions of the servers can lead to different implementation details and timings for the same operations.

name: Thermal Throttling
description: If the servers are operating near their thermal limits, the CPUs may throttle down clock speeds to prevent overheating, leading to inconsistent processing times.

name: System Call Overhead
description: Variations in system call times for the operations the server performs can contribute to the observed latency, especially if the servers are running a different OS version.
